
## This repository is dedicated to show how to make a simple installation of Zabbix in a raspberry machine

## Requirements

- Raspberry Pi 4 (recommended)
- Raspberry Pi OS Lite
- Internet connection
- At least 2 GB RAM
- Sudo privileges

#### First step: Go to [Zabbix download page](https://www.zabbix.com/download) and select your operating system. (In this case, Raspberry OS)
#### Second step: Follow the installation guide automatically generated by the Zabbix website for your selected platform.
This step consist in:
```Install Zabbix repository```,
```Install Zabbix server, frontend, agent2```,
```Install Zabbix agent 2 plugins``` and ``` Create initial database```.

#### Third step: Create initial database
*Note: If you do not already have a database installed on your machine, install MySQL/MariaDB first by following this [MariaDB installation guide](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/mariadb-quickstart-guides/installing-mariadb-server-guide)*

AAfter completing the previous installation steps, it is time to configure the database for Zabbix.
During this step, the Zabbix installation guide will prompt you to execute commands similar to the following:

``` 
sudo mysql

mysql> create database zabbix character set utf8mb4 collate utf8mb4_bin;
mysql> create user zabbix@localhost identified by 'password'; (Replace 'password'with a password of your choice)
mysql> grant all privileges on zabbix.* to zabbix@localhost;
mysql> set global log_bin_trust_function_creators = 1;
mysql> quit;
```
After that, the installation guide will instruct you to import the database [schema](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/database-schema).
```
zcat /usr/share/zabbix/sql-scripts/mysql/server.sql.gz | mysql --default-character-set=utf8mb4 -uzabbix -p zabbix
```
Now we are going to ```disable the log_bin_trust_function_creators``` option.
When enabled (1), this option allows users to create, alter, or drop stored routines (functions/triggers) without requiring the SUPER privilege.
```
sudo mysql

mysql> set global log_bin_trust_function_creators = 0;
mysql> quit;
```

#### Fourth step: Configure the database for Zabbix server

Edit the following file:

```/etc/zabbix/zabbix_server.conf```.

Use your preferred text editor.
After opening the file, locate the following variable:
```DBPassword=```
If the line is commented out with #, remove the comment and set the password you created in the previous step:
DBPassword=your_password

#### Last step: Start Zabbix server and agent processes and make it start at system boot.
```
systemctl restart zabbix-server zabbix-agent2 apache2
systemctl enable zabbix-server zabbix-agent2 apache2
```

#### Troubleshooting

In case of errors, use the following commands to inspect logs and troubleshoot the installation:
```
sudo systemctl status zabbix-server.service
sudo journalctl -xeu zabbix-server.service
sudo tail -n 30 /var/log/zabbix/zabbix_server.log
```
#### Accessing the Web Interface

Open your browser and navigate to:

```http://your-machine-ip/zabbix```

#### Default credentials
```
Username: Admin
Password: zabbix
```
